name: Derince
title: Derince Port Thickness Measurement | Bulk and Steel Ships
description: Ship thickness measurement at Derince port in the Gulf of Izmit: UTM for bulk carriers, steel and project cargo ships and containers during berth stays.
h1: Ultrasonic Gauging for Ships Alongside at Derince Port
intro: Derince is a rail-linked commercial port on the northern shore of the Gulf of Izmit, taking steel, grain, fertiliser, containers and project cargo for the industrial belt around Kocaeli. Ships stay for days when a hold is being worked slowly, and dry cargoes of this kind wear hold steel. That makes Derince a practical place for hold gauging. Technicians travel from India to the ship, boarding at the berth or by launch at the gulf anchorage.
keywords: gulf of izmit general cargo gauging

highlights.p: Steel coils, billets, rebar and project cargo punish tank tops and lower hold structure. After discharge at Derince the damage can be mapped by ultrasonic readings, which settles whether plates need renewal.

Grain and fertiliser cargoes add corrosion and coating loss. Bulk carriers working these trades at Derince are measured once holds are clean, with the discharge schedule setting the length of the visit.
Derince works cargo that moves on to or from the rail network, so many ships are alongside for longer than a container call. Longer stays allow fuller programmes of hold, deck and tank readings.

port.h: Derince: a general cargo port on the Gulf of Izmit
p: Derince lies on the northern shore of the Gulf of Izmit, east of the Dilovası terminals and not far from the city of Izmit. It is among the older commercial ports in the gulf, built as a state railway port, with a rail connection that still carries cargo to the interior, and it has been extended and operated by private companies in modern times. The water is sheltered, the approach is by pilot, and the quays face an anchorage that fills with ships waiting for berths during busy spells in the industrial gulf.

The cargo list is unusually broad for one port. Steel products, including coils, plate, billets and reinforcing bar, move in and out for the region's mills and fabricators. Grain and animal feed arrive in bulk, fertiliser and chemical products pass through, and containers and project cargo such as machinery and structural components share the quays. Bulk carriers, multipurpose ships, general cargo ships and container ships all call here, along with the occasional ro-ro ship, and rail wagons collect and deliver at the quayside.

These cargoes are the main reason owners gauge at Derince. Steel loaded and discharged by crane damages tank tops and frames with every swing, grain leaves moisture and coating breakdown behind, and fertiliser attacks bare steel. Multipurpose ships and general cargo ships that trade in this way for years accumulate wastage in the lower holds that no visual inspection can quantify. Berth stays here are often longer than at a container terminal, since heavy cargo moves slowly, which gives the superintendent time to measure while the ship works.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged at Derince
p: At the quays, hold work is the core scope. Once a hold is discharged, swept and certified for entry, the team measures tank top plating, lower frames and brackets, hopper plating, coamings and hatch covers, and any plates the surveyor has marked. On multipurpose ships the same approach covers tween decks and the structure that carries heavy lifts. The port's permit and access rules apply, and the agent arranges passes, with the sequence agreed around the cargo plan so holds are not held up.

The gulf anchorage is available for ships waiting for a berth, reached by launch through the agent, and the sheltered water usually allows a longer programme of deck, hatch and ballast tank gauging. Derince has no drydock for larger ships, and the usual route for a docking is to Tuzla or the Altınova yards near the mouth of the gulf, with readings from Derince sent ahead to the yard. The Izmit gulf is covered more widely on its own page, and this port's work is largely hold-centred rather than tanker-centred.
list: Cargo quays — tank tops, lower hold frames, hopper plating and coamings on bulk, multipurpose and general cargo ships after discharge
Steel and project cargo berths — hold and tween-deck structure on ships carrying heavy lifts, with impact damage marked
Grain and fertiliser berths — hold and deck gauging on ships working corrosive and moist cargoes
Container berths — ballast tanks, hatch covers and deck structure on feeders during scheduled calls
Gulf anchorage — deck, hatch and ballast tank gauging on ships awaiting berths, reached by launch
Docking at Tuzla or Altınova — Derince readings carried into the yard's steel estimate

context.h: Port state control and the cargo trades behind Derince
p: Derince falls under the Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU regimes that Turkey participates in, enforced by the harbour master and the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships on steel and grain routes are a regular target for inspectors because of hold condition and hatch cover weathertightness, and findings can become the reason for a gauging request. Class surveyors also ask for readings on plates they consider suspect during renewal surveys of older tonnage.

The commerce behind the port is Turkish industry and agriculture, and the shipowners range from Istanbul bulk operators to small regional companies running multipurpose tonnage. Steel exporters and grain importers often require that holds are in good condition before loading, so a thickness record helps an owner avoid disputes. Ships that go on to EU ports need a current Inventory of Hazardous Materials and report under the EU's carbon rules for those voyages, and Derince calls are a convenient point to refresh the hull record.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Derince
jobs.p: Jobs at Derince nearly always involve holds. A superintendent asks for a defined list of compartments after a steel or grain parcel, we agree access with the agent and the master, and the team works while the berth operation continues elsewhere on the ship. Other jobs support a docking at a nearby yard or a sale of a general cargo ship, and results are given by compartment with the worst areas highlighted.
list: Tank top and lower frame gauging on a multipurpose ship after steel coil discharge, with impact damage and wastage recorded by hold.
Hopper and hold frame readings on a Handysize bulk carrier following grain discharge, ahead of a fertiliser loading.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a general cargo ship after a deficiency was recorded in a previous port.
Ballast tank and deck plating readings on a container feeder during a scheduled call.
Pre-docking gauging on an older bulk carrier at the gulf anchorage, giving the Tuzla or Altınova yard a steel list before arrival.
Pre-purchase gauging on a second-hand multipurpose ship alongside, with the buyer's surveyor attending.

logistics: The team flies into Istanbul, normally to Sabiha Gökçen Airport, and reaches Derince by road along the northern shore of the Gulf of Izmit. The ship's agent arranges port passes, launches for the anchorage and the terminal's permit and gas-free requirements, and receives crew lists, technician certificates and equipment details in advance. Technicians from India need a Turkish visa, so we apply when the call is nominated and keep the validity period wide enough for a slipping berth.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged after a steel cargo at Derince?
faqs.a: Yes, once the hold is discharged, swept and certified for entry. We map tank tops, lower frames and hopper plating, record impact damage and wastage by hold, and give the superintendent a plan marked with the worst areas. The work is sequenced around the cargo plan so the hold is handed back on time.

Not for larger merchant ships. A docking normally happens at Tuzla or at the Altınova yards in Yalova, near the mouth of the gulf. We report Derince readings by compartment so they can go straight to the yard to support its steel estimate and shorten the planning.

faqs.q: How long does a ship stay at Derince?
faqs.a: It varies with the cargo. Heavy and project cargo moves slowly, so stays can run to several days, which suits a fuller hold programme. Container feeders are shorter. We ask the agent for the berth schedule and plan the scope to the time the ship is realistically alongside.

faqs.q: Can ships at the gulf anchorage be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, by launch through the agent. The gulf is sheltered, so transfers are usually practical and longer programmes are realistic, although a ship may be called to the berth at short notice. We agree a priority list with the master so the most important deck, hatch and ballast tank readings come first.
